cards.claim: The authors propose the Transformer, a model architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms and eschews recurrence.
cards.evidence_quote: In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

cards.claim: The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization than recurrent models.
cards.evidence_quote: The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

cards.claim: Recurrent models have an inherently sequential nature that precludes parallelization within training examples.
cards.evidence_quote: This inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths, as memory constraints limit batching across examples.

cards.claim: Attention mechanisms allow modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance in the input or output sequences.
cards.evidence_quote: Attention mechanisms have become an integral part of compelling sequence modeling and transduction models in various tasks, allowing modeling of dependencies without regard to their distance in the input or output sequences [2, 19].

cards.claim: The Transformer reduces the number of operations to relate distant positions to a constant, unlike previous convolutional models where complexity grows with distance.
cards.evidence_quote: In these models, the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary input or output positions grows in the distance between positions... In the Transformer this is reduced to a constant number of operations

cards.claim: The authors claim the Transformer is the first transduction model that relies entirely on self-attention without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.
cards.evidence_quote: To the best of our knowledge, however, the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations of its input and output without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.

cards.claim: Self-attention relates different positions of a single sequence to compute a representation of that sequence.
cards.evidence_quote: Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.

cards.claim: Previous convolutional models like ConvS2S and ByteNet make it difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions because operation count grows with distance.
cards.evidence_quote: This makes it more difficult to learn dependencies between distant positions [12].

cards.claim: The Transformer model uses a stacked self-attention and point-wise fully connected layer architecture for both its encoder and decoder.
cards.evidence_quote: The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder

cards.claim: The encoder consists of a stack of N=6 identical layers, each containing multi-head self-attention and a position-wise feed-forward network with residual connections.
cards.evidence_quote: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers. The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism, and the second is a simple, position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.

cards.claim: The proposed Scaled Dot-Product Attention is faster and more space-efficient than additive attention because it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code.
cards.evidence_quote: While the two are similar in theoretical complexity, dot-product attention is much faster and more space-efficient in practice, since it can be implemented using highly optimized matrix multiplication code.

cards.claim: The model employs h=8 parallel attention heads, each with dimension dk=dv=64, to allow the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces simultaneously.
cards.evidence_quote: In this work we employ h = 8 parallel attention layers, or heads. For each of these we use dk = dv = dmodel/h = 64.

cards.claim: The proposed model relies entirely on attention mechanisms, specifically self-attention in both encoder and decoder, replacing recurrence and convolutions.
cards.evidence_quote: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence, we must inject some information about the relative or absolute position of the tokens in the sequence.

cards.claim: The encoder uses self-attention layers where keys, values, and queries come from the previous layer's output, allowing each position to attend to all positions.
cards.evidence_quote: The encoder contains self-attention layers. In a self-attention layer all of the keys, values and queries come from the same place, in this case, the output of the previous layer in the encoder.

cards.claim: The authors chose sinusoidal positional encodings because they hypothesize this allows the model to easily learn attention by relative positions.
cards.evidence_quote: We chose this function because we hypothesized it would allow the model to easily learn to attend by relative positions, since for any fixed offset k, PEpos+k can be represented as a linear function of PEpos.

cards.claim: Self-attention layers connect all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas recurrent layers require O(n) sequential operations.
cards.evidence_quote: a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations.

cards.claim: Self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d.
cards.evidence_quote: In terms of computational complexity, self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d

cards.claim: A single convolutional layer does not connect all pairs of input and output positions, requiring a stack of O(n/k) or O(logk(n)) layers to do so.
cards.evidence_quote: A single convolutional layer with kernel width k < n does not connect all pairs of input and output positions. Doing so requires a stack of O(n/k) convolutional layers

cards.claim: Self-attention could yield more interpretable models, with attention heads learning to perform different tasks related to syntactic and semantic structure.
cards.evidence_quote: As side benefit, self-attention could yield more interpretable models. We inspect attention distributions from our models and present and discuss examples in the appendix.

cards.claim: The Transformer (base model) achieved a BLEU score of 27.3 on English-to-German translation.
cards.evidence_quote: Transformer (base model) 27.3

cards.claim: The Transformer (big model) achieved a BLEU score of 41.8 on English-to-French translation.
cards.evidence_quote: Transformer (big) 28.4 41.8

cards.claim: The authors used the Adam optimizer with specific beta values and epsilon for training.
cards.evidence_quote: We used the Adam optimizer [20] with β1 = 0.9, β2 = 0.98 and ϵ = 10−9.

cards.claim: Label smoothing was employed during training to improve accuracy and BLEU score despite hurting perplexity.
cards.evidence_quote: During training, we employed label smoothing of value ϵls = 0.1 [36]. This hurts perplexity, as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score.

cards.claim: The big Transformer model achieved a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation, outperforming previous best models by more than 2.0 BLEU.
cards.evidence_quote: On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, the big transformer model (Transformer (big) in Table 2) outperforms the best previously reported models (including ensembles) by more than 2.0 BLEU, establishing a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4.

cards.claim: On WMT 2014 English-to-French translation, the big Transformer model achieved a BLEU score of 41.0, outperforming all previously published single models at less than one-quarter the training cost.
cards.evidence_quote: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, our big model achieves a BLEU score of 41.0, outperforming all of the previously published single models, at less than 1/4 the training cost of the previous state-of-the-art model.

cards.claim: The Transformer model generalizes well to English constituency parsing, achieving a semi-supervised F1 score of 92.7 on WSJ Section 23, which is higher than the previous state-of-the-art of 92.1.
cards.evidence_quote: Transformer (4 layers) semi-supervised 92.7

cards.claim: Reducing the attention key size dk hurts model quality, suggesting that determining compatibility is difficult and a more sophisticated function than dot product may be beneficial.
cards.evidence_quote: In Table 3 rows (B), we observe that reducing the attention key size dk hurts model quality. This suggests that determining compatibility is not easy and that a more sophisticated compatibility function than dot product may be beneficial.

cards.claim: The Transformer model achieves better results than all previously reported models except for the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar.
cards.evidence_quote: yielding better results than all previously reported models with the exception of the Recurrent Neural Network Grammar [8].

cards.claim: The Transformer outperforms the Berkeley-Parser even when trained only on the WSJ training set of 40K sentences.
cards.evidence_quote: the Transformer outperforms the Berkeley-Parser [29] even when training only on the WSJ training set of 40K sentences.

cards.claim: The Transformer is the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention.
cards.evidence_quote: In this work, we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing the recurrent layers most commonly used in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-headed self-attention.

cards.claim: The Transformer achieves a new state of the art on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: On both WMT 2014 English-to-German and WMT 2014 English-to-French translation tasks, we achieve a new state of the art.

cards.claim: The Transformer can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers.
cards.evidence_quote: For translation tasks, the Transformer can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers.

cards.claim: The authors plan to extend the Transformer to other modalities like images and audio and investigate local attention mechanisms.
cards.evidence_quote: We plan to extend the Transformer to problems involving input and output modalities other than text and to investigate local, restricted attention mechanisms to efficiently handle large inputs and outputs such as images, audio and video.

rejected.claim: Each layer includes a position-wise feed-forward network consisting of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation, using dimensions d_model=512 and d_ff=2048.
rejected.evidence_quote: This consists of two linear transformations with a ReLU activation in between. The dimensionality of input and output is dmodel = 512, and the inner-layer has dimensionality dff = 2048.
